question: Where does the 512x512 full-aperture Metal SSB phase-variance objective actually spend its time, what is the practical bandwidth ceiling it runs against, and which of the proposed accelerations (cache-layout transpose, phase-batch retuning, multi-candidate fusion) survive an interleaved A/B/A measurement on real ARINA data?

code.note: profile-gates.patch adds env-gated SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_{COLUMN,ROWS,NYQUIST} and SSB_PHASE_BATCH. It is temporary instrumentation only; it is NOT present in the landed source and was reverted before any commit.

parameters.scope: Kernel-level real-data measurement through the scheduling probe. Not a frame-rate or application claim.

execution.gpu_model: Apple M5 10-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory
execution.contention_note: The host was shared with two other agents running swift-frontend compiles and a Python fixture build during the first half of this session (load average 4.3-7.4). All accepted/rejected comparisons are interleaved A/B/A so both arms see the same conditions. The final baseline was re-measured at load average 2.3-2.6. Separately, runs made while three agents each held ~11 GB on a 24 GB machine show 20-69 s stalls concentrated in the first calls of a phase (seq-c pure_loss gpu_ms 37702,61847,64155,38296,38183,68800,31062,38642,31240,1218 then 254-269 ms for the remainder; aba-c2 59407,42060,49655,49015,41072,50318,23554 then 252-299 ms). These are host memory-pressure stalls, not a property of the kernels: they are absent from the quiet runs, where every loss call lands in 262-283 ms.

baseline_quiet_gpu_ms.redraw_first_call_note: The first reconstruct after prepare costs 207-797 ms (lazy pipeline creation and first-touch); the p95 above is that first call. Steady-state redraw min is 79.3-79.8 ms.

loss_pass_ablation_ratio.method: SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_COLUMN / SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_ROWS / both, with SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_NYQUIST as the floor
loss_pass_ablation_ratio.note: A second ablation on the quieter machine had full p50 309.97 vs its own repeat 248.51 ms (25% spread), so only the internally consistent first run is used for the ratio. Absolute values scale with host load; the ordering is stable across both runs.

bandwidth_verdict.pure_read_reference: 9.39 GB G-cache read in 77.58 ms, recorded in 20260911-ssb-fft-intermediate; independently re-derived here from redraw 9.41 GB / 79.3 ms = 118.7 GB/s
bandwidth_verdict.note: Byte accounting and achieved GB/s agree within 10% with the machine's streaming-read ceiling, so the objective spends its time moving bytes rather than in arithmetic.

rejected_arms.change: setCacheColumnMajor encoded one command buffer per cache chunk instead of one per 32-term batch (288 CPU/GPU waits removed).
rejected_arms.reason: Neutral. The transpose is not synchronization-bound: 37.6 GB (9.41 read + 9.41 kernel write + 9.41 blit read + 9.41 blit write) at the machine's ~121 GB/s streaming rate predicts 311 ms, matching the measured 335 ms. The arm was reverted.

rejected_arms.change: Smaller blocked-fftA working set per dispatch (4.2 MB instead of 8.4 MB) to try to keep the intermediate nearer the cache.
rejected_arms.reason: pb4 is 1.1% slower than pb8 once interleaved. An earlier single-pass sweep that showed pb4 264.9 vs pb8 276.0 ms was run-to-run drift. Reverted.

rejected_arms.parity: Losses are bit-identical to pb8 at all of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 (max absolute difference 0.0 across all six evaluations).
rejected_arms.reason: pb2 loses 24% to dispatch count; pb16/pb32 gain no time despite removing up to 3.4 GB of phase-sum traffic, confirming the limit is streaming bandwidth rather than phase-sum writes. No change.

Invalid configuration, not a candidate: 64 terms need 67.4 MB of blocked fftA but the engine allocates 67.1 MB (batchCapacity 32 x 512 x 512 x 8), so the intermediate overruns the workspace and the loss changes by 7.6e-4. Recorded so the ceiling is explicit.

rejected_arms.arm: multi-candidate fused objective (K candidates per pass)
rejected_arms.reason: Bounded, not refuted, and not attempted. The objective is bandwidth-bound, so the only gain is the K-fold amortization of the 9.41 GB G-cache read: traffic falls from 32.71 GB to 23.31 + 9.41/K GB, i.e. 0.785x at K=4 and 0.749x at K=8 in the ideal limit, and the intermediate and phase-sum traffic (23.3 GB) cannot be amortized at all because both are candidate-specific. That bounds the fit saving at roughly 64.5 s -> 50.6 s at K=4, before the register and occupancy cost of K live intermediates. Implementing a K-way fused column pass with exact per-candidate parity needs K chi/cross tables, K blocked intermediates and K phase-sum buffers, and could not be validated inside this session.

rejected_arms.arm: unified single cache layout (remove the transpose)
rejected_arms.reason: This is the largest measured single cost and the recommended next step. setCacheColumnMajor re-lays out the whole 9.41 GB cache because ssb_correct_half_column_ifft512_hermitian reads [bf][col][row] while ssb_gamma_accumulate_half reads [bf][row][col]. Measured cost is ~335 ms of untracked time on every redraw<->loss switch, i.e. more than the loss kernel itself. Removing it requires re-indexing the redraw accumulator's orbit enumeration (ssb.metal:648) so consecutive threads advance in row, which is a delicate rewrite of the paired/boundary enumeration and was not attempted without a full parity campaign.

rejected_arms.arm: hoist the per-chunk switch out of load_g_cache_chunk
rejected_arms.reason: Not supported by the profile. The switch operand is uniform across a threadgroup (it depends only on the bright-field index), so it is a uniform, predicted branch; the row pass already runs within 5-10% of the streaming ceiling. No evidence of a branch cost worth removing.

Not exercised by this workload. With cache_budget_bytes unset the engine admits all 8937 terms, so cachedBrightfieldCount == activeBrightfieldIndices.count and the streamed loop at MetalSSBKernels.swift:710 never runs. The phaseVariance streamed path already windows 32 command buffers (MetalSSBKernels.swift:183). The per-batch commitAndWait at MetalSSBKernels.swift:732 is real but is on the non-cached path only.

historical_discrepancy.verdict: Partially stale, and the remainder is explained by source drift plus host contention. Same-machine same-input comparison against these runs was not possible because the recorded entrypoint is a probe run whose code revision 31717e6 does not contain the accepted blocked-4 scheduler (git grep shows no ssb_intermediate_block_rows at that revision), so the 222.73 ms figure is a dirty-tree prototype measurement. Between 31717e6 and 597b566 both hot kernels changed: the row pass moved from the pre-blocked row-major enumeration to the blocked 4-row tile with prefetch, and it lost the positive-DC fast path (atan of a precomputed reciprocal, ssb.metal old revision) in favour of unconditional atan2 (ssb.metal:1363). The nyquist-correction kernel (ssb.metal:1200, ~11 ms) was also added. The residual gap is host load: the same pristine binary measured loss p50 310 ms at load average 4.3-7.4 and 269-279 ms at load average 2.3-2.6.

results.limits: No binning, cropping, BF reduction, reduced precision, fast-math, or CPU fallback. The loss path never crosses the host: all sums are accumulated in device buffers and reduced on the host only at the end. The fit is 200 sequential single-candidate objective evaluations. XCTest is not runnable on this host (no XCTest module), so the swift test gate was not executed.

outputs.result: Pristine 597b566 probe: redraw gpu p50 84.42 ms, loss gpu p50 271.64 / p95 283.26 ms, prepare 2.15 s, load 2.16 s, 11.37 GB allocated; losses bit-identical to every other run.
Pristine probe repeat: redraw gpu p50 85.53 ms, loss gpu p50 269.37 ms; confirms the baseline is reproducible and that the first redraw after prepare (207-797 ms) is a warm-up outlier.
Pristine probe with fit: 64.54 s for 200 global trials plus 27 Nelder-Mead refinements, best loss 0.1376979947090149; 200 trials x ~272 ms accounts for the search time.

Pass ablation (SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_* gates from profile-gates.patch): full 390.59, no-column 177.47, no-rows 212.98, no-nyquist 362.46, nyquist-only 11.11 ms p50. Derived split column 201.9 / row 166.4 / nyquist 11.1 ms, additive check 379.4 ms.
Interleaved A/B/A/B of the single-command-buffer transpose: untracked p50 base 333.4 and 349.4 ms vs candidate 337.4 and 341.2 ms. Neutral, arm reverted.
Interleaved A/B/A phaseBatch 8 vs 4: loss p50 pb8 273.33/269.44/269.73, pb4 272.60/276.02/268.83 ms; pb4 is 1.1% slower. Losses bit-identical at 0.14511984586715698.

Alternation probe. With the cache layout stable, wall-minus-command-buffer time is 1.5 ms; on every redraw<->loss switch it is 334-447 ms, isolating the 9.41 GB cache-layout transpose as a real per-switch cost. The 20-69 s entries in some runs are host memory-pressure stalls in the first calls of a phase, not per-batch synchronization; that was tested separately and refuted.
